title: These 2 Consumer Staples Stocks Could Beat Earnings: Why They Should Be on Your Radar
author: Zacks.Com
description: Zacks identifies two consumer staples stocks with positive Earnings Surprise Prediction (ESP) metrics that could potentially beat upcoming earnings expectations. General Mills (GIS) has a +0.94% ESP ahead of its December 16, 2026 earnings report, while Kimberly-Clark (KMB) shows a +0.56% ESP before reporting on January 26, 2027. Both stocks hold a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Positive Earnings ESP of +0.94% indicates the Most Accurate Estimate ($0.97) exceeds the Zacks Consensus Estimate ($0.96), suggesting potential for an earnings beat. Historical data shows stocks with positive ESP produce positive surprises 70% of the time.

Positive Earnings ESP of +0.56% indicates the Most Accurate Estimate ($1.70) exceeds the Zacks Consensus Estimate ($1.69), suggesting potential for an earnings beat. The positive ESP metric aligns with the same predictive framework as GIS.

title: A Once-in-a-Decade Opportunity: 1 Magnificent Dividend Stock Down 30% to Buy Right Now
author: Micah Zimmerman
description: General Mills stock has fallen 30% from its 52-week high, offering a 7% dividend yield. Despite near-term challenges from consumer spending pressures and margin squeezes, the company is showing signs of recovery through new product innovations like protein cereals and dye-free options. With 128 years of uninterrupted dividend payments and new leadership taking over, the stock appears undervalued at 11x expected earnings.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock is trading at a significant discount (30% below 52-week high) with an attractive 7% dividend yield. The company demonstrates resilience through successful product innovations (protein cereals growing double-digit, Lucky Charms recovery, Pillsbury reformulation), maintains a 128-year dividend payment history, and has a clear cost-reduction strategy ($3B by 2030). New CEO appointment and improving pet food segment add confidence, though near-term earnings pressure and margin challenges exist.

title: Can General Mills' New Operating Model Drive Profitable Growth?
author: Na
description: General Mills announced a major restructuring effective January 1, 2027, consolidating operations into three segments: Cereal, Snacks & International; Meals & Baking Solutions; and Pet. The company will also establish a centralized commercial function to improve efficiency and decision-making. GIS targets $750 million in cost savings for fiscal 2027 and at least $3 billion by fiscal 2030, though recent performance showed flat organic sales and declining operating profit.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While the restructuring demonstrates management's commitment to improving efficiency and long-term profitability, recent financial results show flat organic sales and declining operating profit. The stock trades at a discount valuation (P/E 11.07 vs. industry 14.83), suggesting market skepticism. The restructuring is a positive strategic move, but execution risks and near-term headwinds warrant a neutral stance.

Luckin Coffee holds a Zacks Rank #1 with projected sales growth of 33.3% and earnings growth of 48.4%, demonstrating strong momentum and expansion potential in the Chinese beverage market.
Smucker carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with expected fiscal-year earnings growth of 17.1% and a solid trailing four-quarter earnings surprise average of 13.8%, indicating reliable performance.

title: 3 Magnificent High-Yield Dividend Stocks to Buy Near Their 52-Week Lows
author: Justin Pope
description: PepsiCo, General Mills, and Clorox are trading near 52-week lows with elevated dividend yields due to business challenges. Despite growth headwinds and operational issues, all three maintain viable dividends with solid fundamentals, offering potential value opportunities for dividend investors willing to accept higher risk.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock faces near-term growth challenges from pricing pressures and GLP-1 agonist competition, but maintains strong fundamentals as a Dividend King with 54 consecutive years of raises. Trading at attractive valuation (18x vs 10-year average of 25x) with sustainable 75% payout ratio offers value for patient investors.

Company faces significant growth challenges with flat organic sales and elevated 7.1% dividend yield signaling distress. While dividend remains viable at 85% payout ratio, the stock is riskier than typical dividend plays. Turnaround potential exists through cost-cutting and portfolio restructuring, but execution risk is high.

Recent operational challenges (cybersecurity breach, ERP transition) have pressured the stock, but core business remains solid with category-leading products. GOJO acquisition provides growth opportunities. Currently spending over 100% of cash flow on dividends, but this appears temporary. Nearly a Dividend King with 49 consecutive years of raises.

title: General Mills Has Paid Uninterrupted Dividends for 127 Years. Here's the Yearly Payout on $5,000.
author: Jack Delaney
description: General Mills offers an attractive 6.8% dividend yield with 127 years of uninterrupted payouts, translating to roughly $334 annually on a $5,000 investment. However, the stock has declined 21% in 2026 due to slowing sales and the company's struggle to adapt to changing consumer preferences toward healthier options. The author recommends avoiding General Mills in favor of alternatives like Kimberly-Clark, Procter & Gamble, or Coca-Cola that offer both reliable dividends and better growth potential.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Despite a high 6.8% dividend yield and 127 years of uninterrupted dividends, the company faces significant headwinds including a 21% stock decline in 2026, 5% revenue decline in fiscal 2026, and ongoing struggles to adapt to consumer preferences for healthier foods. The author explicitly recommends avoiding the stock.
